current: ## Intended outcome
proposed:
## Problem

A customer contacts the Bank several times about the same issue. Calls, chats, cases, complaints and status changes sit in separate records. The employee has to reconstruct the history by hand and may miss the actual blocker, repeat an earlier request or transfer the customer again.

## Intended outcome
note: The page had no problem statement. Text is the "Problem" paragraph of the source proposal, with "the Bank" capitalized.

locator: Second paragraph under "## Intended outcome"
current: The employee reviews the interpretation, owns the response and approves any operational action. AI-generated interpretations remain distinguishable from verified facts.
proposed:
The employee reviews the interpretation, owns the response and approves any operational action. AI-generated interpretations remain distinguishable from verified facts.

Customer intelligence here means the reusable result of that work: a source-linked record of the customer's service history, the action taken and its outcome, kept for the stated purpose and available to later service journeys.

## What would be built

For each eligible case the employee sees the customer's current request, a short timeline of earlier contacts and actions, the verified current status, the likely reason the issue is still open, the approved procedure with the proposed next step, and links to the underlying records. The likely reason is marked as an inference.

Banking systems remain the source of facts. A context service assembles the minimum authorized view for the journey, an assistant with limited authority interprets it within a fixed workflow, and the employee decides. AI does not establish customer identity, payment status, eligibility, deadlines or permissions.
note: The title promises "customer intelligence" and the page never explained it; the page also never said what would be built. Both paragraphs condense the source proposal ("What is built", "Target pilot architecture", "Where GenAI adds value").
